feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: Explore scientific breakthroughs, space discoveries, research trends and everyday mysteries with NPR’s science team. Plus episodes from the Short Wave podcast.

entry.title: More people are getting the flu. Should you get a flu shot before you travel?
entry.summary: Thanksgiving is just around the corner, just as millions of Americans are expected to travel for the holidays. Another thing that's upon us? Cold and flu season.

entry.title: Brain cell mapping lays groundwork for better treatments for conditions like dementia
entry.summary: A major effort from brain researchers around the world has yielded a cellular atlas of the basal ganglia — structures key to learning and controlling motor skills.

entry.title: Far from home, Voyager 1 will soon be a 'light-day' from Earth
entry.summary: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest human-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.

entry.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
entry.summary: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.

entry.title: SpaceX deploys Starlink satellites in Starship test, but booster crashes into Gulf
entry.summary: SpaceX conducted a major test of its Starship rocket Friday night. It deployed several satellites for the Starlink constellation, but there was a problem with its booster.

entry.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
entry.summary: New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.

entry.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
entry.summary: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station.

entry.title: This week in science: PTSD prediction, phishing while tired, an exoplanet
entry.summary: The regular news roundup with NPR's science podcast Short Wave covers a possible use for AI in emergency rooms, a distant planet and the link between cybersecurity and Daylight Saving Time.

entry.title: Scientists think they've found ancient remnants of dinosaur blood
entry.summary: Scientists have studied plenty of dinosaur bones, eggs and footprints. Now, some think they've found their strongest evidence yet of dinosaur blood.

entry.title: Mice can learn to fight by watching tiny rodent cage matches, study finds
entry.summary: Brain scientists set up "gladiator style" cage matches for mice — and found that simply observing fighting matches can rewire a mouse's brain to resemble those who actually fought.
